2027 Kia Sorento PHEV Drops Cheaper Trim, X-Line SX-Prestige Gets $400 Pricier
8 photos
Photo: Kia
The priciest Sorento for the US market is even pricier for 2027. Kia America decided to stop selling the cheaper grade, leaving the loaded X-Line SX-Prestige AWD as the only choice at $53,890 before the $1,495 destination charge. $400 pricier than before, the Sorento PHEV X-Line SX-Prestige adds one item as standard for 2027, specifically a head-up display.
Last year's EX with all-wheel drive used to retail at $48,290 from the outset, meaning that the 2027 model is a staggering $5,600 more expensive. You do get plenty of equipment for the money, beginning with the head-up display mentioned earlier. Customers who want the plug further get a heated steering wheel, heated second-row seats, and a panoramic sunroof.
Goodies also include ventilated and heated front seats, perforated leather across all three rows, 14-way power adjustments and a thigh extension for the driver's seat, 10-way power adjustments for the front passenger, second-row captain's chairs, and a split-folding third row for a grand total of six seats. X-Line embossing on the front seatbacks also needs mentioning, along with open-pore inlays.
The people sitting behind the first row are presented with retractable sunshades, while audio entertainment comes courtesy of a 12-speaker Bose system. Wireless phone charging and a power liftgate come along for the ride. Good for 31 miles (50 kilometers) of electric-only driving, the plug-in hybrid Sorento for the US market is equipped with a battery that nets just around 14 kilowatt-hours.
A Level 1/Level 2 charging cable is included, which is great to hear when the entire point of the Sorento PHEV involves plugging in. Instead of an eCVT, a six-speed tranny does the talking. Under the hood, you will find a familiar 1.6-liter turbocharged inline-four that wouldn't mean too much without electric assistance.
Photo: Kia Kia America says the combined output is 268 horsepower, with peak torque rated at 270 pound-feet (366 Newton-meters) in optimal conditions. The specifications sheet also reads 8.6 seconds to 62 miles per hour (100 kilometers per hour), 74 miles per gallon equivalent with electric assistance, and 33 miles per gallon (7.1 liters per 100 kilometers) for gas-only operation.
With a full tank of gas and a full charge of the high-voltage battery, the Sorento PHEV should be good for a combined range of 440 miles (708 kilometers). The X-Line treatment dresses the nicely equipped SX-Prestige with 19-inch wheels, darker exterior detailing, specific bumpers, and so forth. Also worth noting, Steel Gray is out in favor of Pale Gray in the paint color palette.
Offering nearly 7.0 inches (176 millimeters) of ground clearance, the Sorento PHEV is pretty smart as well, offering Highway Driving Assist 2 and rear parking collision avoidance. Techy highlights also include surround view and blind-spot monitoring. Of course, adaptive cruise control is a standard item as well.
The compact-ish third row of seats brings a compromise to the table, with Kia America listing 29.6 inches (752 millimeters) of legroom and 12.6 cubic feet (357 liters) of cargo space behind it. Folding the rearmost seats for a four-seat layout, cargo volume increases to anything from 38.5 to 45.0 cubic feet (1,090 to 1,274 liters).
